quote_zh: Process Variant A): In a 1 I stirred apparatus, 100g of 2-chloro-3-methyl4-sulfonylmethylbenzoic acid were suspended in 400 ml of chlorobenzene. At room temperature, 85.9 g of N-bromosuccinimide and 6.6 g of azoisobutyroniltrile were added and the mixture was subsequently heated to 60° C. Afterwards, 2.6 g of bromine were added and the reaction mixture was further heated gradually to 90° C. The mixture was stirred at 90° C. for 2 h; after this time, HPLC analysis indicated a conversion of more than 98%. After the reaction mixture had been cooled, 100 ml of a 2% sodium bisulfite solution and 400 ml of water were added in succession and stirred well. The suspension was filtered, and the solid was washed and dried at 60° C. under reduced pressure. 121.3 g (88.4% of theory) of 3-bromomethyl-2-chloro4-methylsulfonyl-benzoic acid were obtained. Purity: 96% (HPLC) Melting point: 207-208° C.
arithmetic_check: IT CLOSES, EXACTLY, AND NOTHING IS FLAGGED. No mole figure is printed anywhere in this step, so there is no mass/mole pair to test and molar_mass_inconsistent cannot arise. Substrate: 2-chloro-3-methyl-4-methylsulfonylbenzoic acid is C9H9ClO4S, MW 9(12.011) + 9(1.008) + 35.453 + 4(15.999) + 32.06 = 248.68; 100 g is 0.40212 mol. Product: 3-bromomethyl-2-chloro-4-methylsulfonylbenzoic acid is C9H8BrClO4S, MW 327.58, the substrate less one hydrogen plus one bromine (79.904 - 1.008 = 78.90, and 248.68 + 78.90 = 327.58). One bromine enters the side-chain methyl, so the transformation is one to one and the theoretical product is 0.40212 x 327.58 = 131.73 g. Stated isolate: 121.3 g at the stated 96% HPLC purity is 121.3 x 0.96 = 116.45 g of the named compound. Closure: 116.45 / 131.73 = 0.88400, i.e. 88.40% of theory, against the 88.4% printed at line 124. Agreement to three significant figures. Note that the crude 121.3 g uncorrected for purity would be 92.1% of theory, so the printed 88.4% is only reproducible once the printed 96% purity is applied, which is itself evidence that the two printed figures were computed against each other and against the correctly ordered methylsulfonyl structure rather than the as-printed sulfonylmethyl one. Reagent stoichiometry, checked for plausibility rather than flagged: 85.9 g of N-bromosuccinimide, MW 177.99, is 0.4826 mol, 1.20 equivalents against the substrate; 2.6 g of bromine, MW 159.81, is 0.0163 mol, 0.040 equivalents, consistent with the text's use of it as an accelerant alongside the N-bromosuccinimide rather than as the brominating charge; 6.6 g of azoisobutyronitrile, MW 164.21, is 0.0402 mol, 0.100 equivalents, a tenth of a mole of initiator per mole of substrate. Nothing is sub-stoichiometric in a way the text does not support and nothing exceeds what the substrate could consume. VERDICT: mass_balance_implausible is NOT raised, molar_mass_inconsistent is NOT raised, scale_discontinuity is NOT raised (no prior step feeds this one), and validation_flags is empty. Per A2 rule 29's second half, a step whose arithmetic closes gets no flag; inventing one here would be a false finding and would send a reviewer to a page where there is nothing to see.

No [IMAGE_EXTRACT: ...] span falls anywhere inside lines 114 to 131; the nearest spans are at line 102, before the section, and at lines 144 and 146, after it. After a further 2 h of irradiation, the reaction mixture had been substantially decolorized. According to HPLC analysis, the reaction mixture contained 87% of product and 10% of reactant.

quote_zh: In a 0.5 I stirred apparatus, 20 g of 2-chloro-3-methyl-4-sulfonylethylbenzoic acid were suspended in 150 ml of acetonitrile. At room temperature, 17.6 g of N-bromosuccinimide and 0.7 g of dibenzoyl peroxide were added and the mixture was subsequently heated to reflux. After in each case 1 h, further dibenzoyl peroxide was added in 3 portions each of 0.7 g and the mixture was stirred for a further 2 h after the last addition. After this time, HPLC analysis indicated complete conversion. After the reaction mixture had been cooled, 100 ml of a 2% sodium bisulfite solution and 300 ml of ethyl acetate were added in succession. The organic phase was removed, washed and concentrated under reduced pressure. The solid residue was suspended in 50 ml of diethyl ether and 20 ml of heptane, filtered off and dried. 28.2 g (95.6% of theory) of 3-bromomethyl-2-chloro-4-ethylsulfonylbenzoic acid were obtained. Purity: 88% (HPLC) Melting point: 103° C.
arithmetic_check: It closes, once the stated purity is applied, so nothing is raised. Stated input: 20 g of the substrate 2-chloro-3-methyl-4-ethylsulfonylbenzoic acid, C10H11ClO4S, MW 262.70, which is 0.07613 mol. The patent states no mole figure; this one is computed here. Stated output: 28.2 g of 3-bromomethyl-2-chloro-4-ethylsulfonylbenzoic acid, C10H10BrClO4S, MW 341.60, at 88% purity by HPLC, with a printed yield of 95.6% of theory. Taken at face value the 28.2 g alone is 0.08255 mol, which is 108.4% of the 0.07613 mol charged and therefore impossible, so the printed yield cannot be a raw mass yield. Purity-corrected, 28.2 g at 88% is 24.82 g, or 0.07265 mol, giving 95.42% of theory against the 95.6% printed. The two agree to within rounding, which confirms that the patent's stated yield is purity-corrected. Both mass_balance_implausible and molar_mass_inconsistent are therefore correctly absent: the mass/mole pairs imply exactly the molecular weights of the compounds named, and this also independently confirms the ethylsulfonyl reading of the substrate name, since the sulfonylethyl misprint would name the same formula but the Example 1 methylsulfonyl homologue, MW 248.7 and 327.6, does not fit these masses. Secondary checks, all consistent, none stated by the patent: 17.6 g of N-bromosuccinimide, MW 177.98, is 0.09888 mol or 1.30 equivalents, a normal slight excess for a benzylic bromination; dibenzoyl peroxide, MW 242.23, totals 2.8 g over four 0.7 g portions, which is 0.01156 mol or 0.152 equivalents overall and 0.038 equivalents per portion, an initiator loading and not a stoichiometric charge. The 2.8 g total is arithmetic on the printed 0.7 g and 3 portions; the patent never prints the total, which is why the record itself carries only the printed 0.7 g single charge in quantity.mass_g and the computed total stays here, where computed figures belong. The 100 ml of 2% sodium bisulfite solution is a volume of solution, so no mass of the salt can be derived and none was. Time, computed here for the same reason the initiator total is. The section prints four intervals, 1 h, 1 h and 1 h between the four initiator portions and then a further 2 h after the last addition, which sum to 5 h at reflux. That 5 h is arithmetic on printed intervals and the digit 5 appears nowhere in [0033] or [0034], so it stays in this sidecar: conditions.time_h on the record carries the printed final 2 h, and the interval structure is carried in words in the record's notes and in the initiator's addition_profile. An earlier version of the record put the 5.0 total in time_h, which is the same class of defect as the 2.8 g initiator total, and both are now confined to this field.
